question: Should OpenClaw establish a core persisted session-chain contract now, and if so should its canonical root/trace identity be owned by SessionEntry or by TaskFlow/orchestration state?
rationale: The requested fields become durable cross-surface API and state semantics; source-level mechanics cannot determine the intended identity model or prevent duplicate ownership.

options.title: Adopt a session-chain contract
options.body: Define SessionEntry as the canonical owner of immutable parent, root, trace, and depth metadata, with TaskFlow consuming rather than duplicating it.

options.title: Make TaskFlow canonical
options.body: Keep session rows limited to existing local lineage and design the chain identity in TaskFlow before exposing a new session API.

options.title: Defer the contract
options.body: Retain the existing parent/depth and ACP projections until a concrete multi-hop debugging or UI consumer establishes the required public shape.

recommendation.title: Adopt a session-chain contract
recommendation.body: Define SessionEntry as the canonical owner of immutable parent, root, trace, and depth metadata, with TaskFlow consuming rather than duplicating it.

likelyOwner.reason: The available issue triage and recent central session/gateway history place this ownership decision closest to this area.
